system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

content.text:
# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: AWS
G2: GCP
G3: software development
G4: Go beyond terratest

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Filling the 2020-2022 or 2024 gaps with invented jobs or stretching neighbouring date ranges
T2: Disclosing more private/medical detail than needed (father's death) instead of a neutral 'career break' if anything
T3: Claiming AWS or GCP for multi-cloud ads
T4: Calling him a software developer or claiming Python/Go development
T5: Old cover letter targets an IT Administrator job and says 'available to start immediately' - no longer true
T6: The CV lists skills first; writer should keep dates accurate when reordering

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer
Rotterdam, Netherlands | samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud and infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing and operating Microsoft Azure
environments, developing Terraform infrastructure modules, migrating Azure IaaS workloads, and
automating application release pipelines with Azure DevOps. Experienced with Linux and Windows
servers, virtual machines, landing-zone networking, identity administration, and practical security
baselines.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud: Microsoft Azure (VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure AD / Entra ID)
Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and Automation: Terraform, Bicep, Ansible, PowerShell, Bash
Platforms and Containers: Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), Docker, Kubernetes (AKS)
CI/CD: Azure DevOps Pipelines
Networking and Security: TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, MFA, conditional access
Identity and Productivity: Active Directory, Microsoft 365 administration
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Cloud Engineer (Contract) Mar 2025 – Present
Havenstad Logistics B.V., Rotterdam
• Work as part of a three-person cloud team operating the company’s Azure estate, comprising
approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters across three subscriptions.
• Developed Terraform infrastructure modules for landing-zone networking, including hub-spoke
VNets, Azure Firewall, and private endpoints.
• Migrated release pipelines for 15 internal applications from manual deployments to Azure DevOps
YAML pipelines.
Freelance IT Administrator Sep 2022 – Jan 2024
Self-employed (Small Businesses)
• Set up and supported Microsoft 365 and Azure AD for nine small businesses with 5–40 employees.
• Migrated two clients from on-premises file servers to SharePoint and OneDrive.
• Configured backups and basic security baselines, including MFA and conditional access.
Systems Administrator Jan 2014 – Feb 2020
Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, Schiedam
• Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting municipal services.
• Led the 2019 lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware-hosted servers to Azure IaaS.
• Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.
• Provided second-line escalation for network and Active Directory issues.
Helpdesk Technician Aug 2011 – Dec 2013
Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
EDUCATION
MBO 4 IT Systems and Networks | Delta Vocational College | 2011
CERTIFICATIONS
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) | 2019
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003) | 2025
LANGUAGES
Dutch (native), English (fluent), Twi (spoken)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role on the Fleet Connectivity
team. I bring hands-on experience designing and operating Azure infrastructure, building
Terraform modules, and moving workloads and release processes into cloud-based environments.
The opportunity to help shape a new train-to-cloud platform from architecture through
production particularly interests me.
In my current contract role at Havenstad Logistics, I work in a three-person team operating an
Azure estate of approximately 400 virtual machines and 12 AKS clusters across three
subscriptions. I designed and developed Terraform modules for landing-zone networking,
including hub-spoke VNets, Azure Firewall and private endpoints, and migrated release
pipelines for 15 internal applications to Azure DevOps YAML. Earlier, I led a lift-and-shift
migration of 60 VMware-hosted servers to Azure IaaS and administered Windows and Linux
systems supporting municipal services.
My experience also includes networking, identity administration and practical security measures,
including MFA, conditional access, backups and firewall configuration. These foundations align
with the role’s focus on secure, reliable and observable infrastructure, including monitoring with
Azure Monitor. My experience designing landing-zone networking and leading infrastructure
migrations would allow me to contribute a methodical infrastructure perspective to
system-design discussions. My cloud experience is with Azure, and I hold the Microsoft
Certified: Azure Administrator Associate and HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate
certifications.
Corvale’s engineering-led approach and emphasis on end-to-end ownership make this role
especially compelling. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience leading
the migration of 60 VMware-hosted servers to Azure IaaS, developing Terraform infrastructure
modules, and modernising 15 application release pipelines could contribute to the Fleet
Connectivity platform.
Kind regards,
Samuel Achterberg-Osei

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
